thread:
Lina: quick check — after yesterday's offload changes i'm still seeing tail OOMs when host-offload happens mid-query. repro: run a 128-token burst across 6 shards with async-drain enabled, sometimes the last microbatch OOMs on gpu0. logs below. :confused:

Lina: ```
[2026-03-22T16:12:01Z] shard0 start microbatch id=42 seq=7
[2026-03-22T16:12:01Z] shard3 offload start page_range=0x7f..
[2026-03-22T16:12:01Z] shard0 error OOM while pinning 24MB
```

Ethan: hmm. do we have a timeline of events? looks like offload start raced with microbatch pin. is async-drain deferring pin until host copy finishes? :thinking:

Lina: timeline is above — offload initiated by eviction scanner, async-drain tries to evict LRU pages but doesn't cancel ongoing pin attempts. pin wins -> OOM if free staging not available.

Priya: iirc our semantics were: async-drain should only win if there are no inflight pins, else it should enqueue a soft-demote. maybe that never landed in allocator-refactor.

Sam: +1 to soft-demote. suggestion: introduce a short lease-window check in the evict path: if page.pin_count > 0 && now - pin_start < 50ms, skip evict and mark a demote_hints list. this avoids aborting an in-flight microbatch.

Marta: another angle — clamp in-flight microbatch tokens per shard. we saw similar tail OOMs with bursty loads; limiting concurrent pins reduces peak staging demand. we can expose a dynamic token_quota that allocator consults before allowing a new pin.

Ethan: both sound good. operational question: if we defer eviction (soft-demote), how do we ensure eventual progress? scheduler could periodically retry demote_hints with exponential backoff. also we should surface demote_hints as telemetry.

Lina: agreed. telemetry would help correlate eviction attempts -> pin races. also need a fallback: if demote_hints backlog gets > N, trigger a conservative global throttle on new microbatches to avoid building unbounded backlog.

Priya: API-wise, we can add a `PinResult` enum: {OK, DEFERRED, BUSY, OOM}. allocator returns DEFERRED when eviction can't proceed; caller can either wait or take a cheaper recompute path.

Sam: small nit — callers (runtime) need a latency SLO budget for waiting on DEFERRED. propose default wait=8ms, then fall back to recompute or fail-open. we already have a `kvcache_recompute` flag in config; tie it in.

Marta: for implementation: patch plan
1) add demote_hints queue + retry worker (per-node)
2) add token_quota check in pin path, configurable per deployment (default small)
3) PinResult enum + short wait path in runtime with observability
4) global backlog guard -> throttle microbatch acceptance if backlog > threshold

Lina: +1 on plan. can someone volunteer a small PoC? i can wire the telemetry and backlog guard once core primitives exist.

Ethan: i'll take the demote_hints queue and retry worker. ETA EOD Friday for a branch.

Priya: i'll add PinResult and runtime wait/fallback. will also add a perf test for the 128-token burst case.

Sam: i'll prototype token_quota clamp and expose knob in the per-shard config. will run load tests against canary.

ops-bot: deploy: canary started — `canary/async-offload-safety-2026-03-22` (rolling across 3 nodes) :rocket:

Lina: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with a short doc linking the new metrics (demote_hints.count, pin_wait.latency, backlog.size) and the suggested default knobs. once PoCs land we'll run the burst microbatch perf job. :thumbsup:
